newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian money dealers see hot summer, no respite.
newsitem.headline: Belgian money dealers see hot summer, no respite.

text.p: Belgian money market dealers said on Wednesday they feared a long hot summer lies ahead of them after this week's rise in market interest rates.

With the Belgian franc at its lowest levels against the mark for more than two years, and worries over neighbouring France's ability to meet the criteria for EMU, the immediate future is bleak. "We're in for a hot summer with no holiday," one said.

Three month T-bills yielded 3.45/49 percent at midday on Wednesday, up from 3.46 percent at Tuesday's auction and levels around 3.29 percent last week. The franc was at 20.6470/85 to the mark. It hit 20.65, its lowest since March 1995, on Monday.

Traders said the National Bank of Belgium was keeping money market liquidity tight to help support the franc, a situation that had been exacerbated by some counterparties being absent from the market for summer holidays.

They did not think that market interest rates were being influenced adversely by the central bank's regular fixing of interest rates on its 230 billion franc CD programme launched last year. The interest rates on the two- and four-month bills are fixed on the basis of average T-bill yields on the two days preceeding any fixing. The latest two month CD rate fixing on Tuesday evening resulted in a rate of 3.42 percent NBBG.
